correctness.rationale: The open 4x4 graph has exactly 24 edges and 36 enumerated perfect matchings. Since each matching contains one edge incident to each vertex, 16 star gauges with one relation reduce all 2^24 Fourier characters to 2^9 signed matching sums. Two distinct exact algorithms, recursive matching enumeration with Walsh transform and 8x8 Kasteleyn determinant with Bareiss elimination, calculate all 512 sums and match the stated multiplicities; Parseval 512*36 is checked. A second exact transform gives the projection-kernel absolute sum 3698, so its exact l1 and linfinity norm is 3698/512=1849/256. The spectral rank 279*32768, gap four, pseudoinverse 1/4, and eight corner singleton zeros follow by Fourier diagonalization and certified counts. Computation is exhaustive with bounded loops, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The 4x4 open-square dimer is a canonical planar matching system with a small yet genuinely nontrivial nine-cycle gauge quotient and 36 coverings. Its complete exact signed partition-function cancellation spectrum discriminates 233 invisible and 279 recoverable gauge modes. The first-cancellation edge geometry and sharp 1849/256 endpoint amplification give a natural complete Fourier recovery benchmark not implied numerically by tiling count 36; the exact finite invariant can be reused to test signed planar-dimer calculations and Fourier reconstruction methods.
